blocks.content: This concluding chapter consolidates key personalities and every important numeric/name/date fact from the preceding chapters into one place for rapid last-minute revision before the exam.

cells: Led the Ulgulan (1899-1900); Jharkhand's most iconic historical figure; state Formation Day and national Janjatiya Gaurav Divas both mark his birth anniversary (Chapters 3-4)
Founder of the Jharkhand Party (1950); captain of India's gold-medal 1928 Olympic hockey team; Constituent Assembly member (Chapter 4)
Co-founder of the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (1972); multiple-time (non-continuous) Chief Minister; father of Hemant Soren (Chapters 4-5)
First Jharkhand CM to complete a full 5-year term (2014-2019) (Chapter 5)
Current (2026) Chief Minister of Jharkhand (JMM), multiple non-continuous stints, current term since 4 July 2024 (Chapter 5)
Visionary founder whose plans led to the establishment of Jamshedpur and Tata Steel (Chapter 6)
Devised the Ol Chiki script for the Santhali language (Chapter 7)

items: Jharkhand: approx 79,714 sq km; dominated by the Chota Nagpur Plateau; borders Bihar, West Bengal, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, UP.
Highest point: Parasnath Hill (~1,365 m) = also Sammed Shikharji, Jainism's most sacred site.
Key rivers: Damodar (DVC-regulated), Subarnarekha, North & South Koel, Barakar.
Mineral hub: Jharia (coking coal), Noamundi/Singhbhum (iron ore, copper), Jaduguda (uranium, India's first), Koderma (mica).
Nagvanshi dynasty gave its name to 'Chota Nagpur'; Chero dynasty ruled from Palamu.
Tribal uprisings, in order: Chuar Rebellion -> Kol Rebellion (1831-32) -> Bhumij Revolt (1832-33) -> Santhal Hul (1855-56) -> Sardari Larai -> Birsa Munda's Ulgulan (1899-1900).
Birsa Munda died in Ranchi jail, 9 June 1900; his movement led to the Chotanagpur Tenancy Act, 1908.
Formed 15 November 2000 (Birsa Munda's birth anniversary) under the Bihar Reorganisation Act, 2000, from 18 southern Bihar districts.
Formed the same year (2000) as Chhattisgarh and Uttarakhand.
81-seat Assembly: 28 ST + 9 SC reserved seats; current CM Hemant Soren (JMM); current Governor Santosh Kumar Gangwar.
Raghubar Das (2014-19) = first CM to complete a full term, after a volatile 2000-2013 period.
Jamshedpur (1907-08, Tata Group) = India's first planned industrial city, home to Tata Steel; Bokaro = major public-sector (SAIL) steel plant.
CNT Act (1908) and SPT Act (1949) = foundational tribal land-protection laws.
Population (2011) approx 3.30 crore; ST share approx 26%; 32 officially recognised Scheduled Tribes; 8 PVTGs.
Santhali written in the Ol Chiki script; included in the Constitution's Eighth Schedule.
Sarhul (spring) and Karma (monsoon) are the flagship tribal festivals; Chhau dance (Seraikella style) is UNESCO-recognised.
Sarna Dharm Code demand remains a live current-affairs issue.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name/date fact from Chapters 1-10 in one place for rapid recall.
The single most important date to never confuse: 15 November — Birsa Munda's birth anniversary, Jharkhand's Formation Day (2000), AND the national Janjatiya Gaurav Divas (since 2021).
Always verify current officeholders (Governor, CM) closer to your exam date, since Jharkhand's political landscape has changed rapidly in recent years.
